name: Torna Fort (Prachandagad)
epithet: स्वराज्याचे तोरण — The First Conquest of Swarajya
shortDesc: First fort captured by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in 1645 at age 16; the highest hill fort in Pune district renamed Prachandagad for its sheer scale.
overviewTitle: The Auspicious Archway Where Hindavi Swarajya Began
overviewP1: Towering at 1,403 meters (4,603 ft) above Velhe taluka, Torna is the highest hill fort in Pune district and the inaugural milestone of Hindavi Swarajya. In 1645, at just 16 years of age, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj captured Torna, hoisting the Bhagwa Dhwaj and renaming the colossal mountain citadel *Prachandagad* ('The Massive Fort').
overviewP2: Famous for its two dramatic knife-edge ridges — the razor-thin Zunjar Machi on the east and the sprawling Budhla Machi on the west — Torna also connects to Rajgad via a legendary high-altitude saddle ridge trek.

architecturalPillars.title: Zunjar Machi Knife-Edge
architecturalPillars.desc: A thrilling rocky spur jutting out from the eastern cliff face, guarded by iron ladders and sheer vertical drops.

architecturalPillars.title: Budhla Machi Ridge
architecturalPillars.desc: Named after its inverted oil-vessel rock pinnacle (Budhla), stretching nearly 2 km with multiple gates including Chincha and Konkan Darwaza.

infobox.quote: While repairing the ramparts of Torna, Mother Bhavani blessed the young Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj with pots of gold mohurs buried in the rock.

sites.name: Zunjar Machi (झुंजार माची)
sites.subtitle: Dramatic Razor-Edge Eastern Bastion Spur
sites.desc: Narrow fortified spur offering breathtaking views of Rajgad's Sanjivani Machi right across the Gunjavane valley.

timeline.title: 1645 — First Conquest of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj
timeline.desc: At age 16, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj captures Torna Fort with his Mavala companions, marking the birth of the sovereign Maratha state.

routes.title: Velhe — Bini Darwaza Ascent
routes.desc: Steep mountain trail from Velhe base village climbing along the northern ridge to Bini Darwaza and Kothi Darwaza.
